name: Refugee Status Determination (CONARE)

requirements.blocker_text: Bolivia has a real domestic refugee law -- Ley No. 251 of 2012 and its implementing Decreto Reglamentario No. 1440/2012 -- administered by CONARE (Comisión Nacional del Refugiado) through its Technical Secretariat (SECONARE). Process, per UNHCR's own Bolivia help portal: file an application (verbally or in writing) within 90 days of entry at a border post, airport, DIGEMIG office, or CONARE headquarters in La Paz, free and personal; receive a free 'Documento Temporal de Solicitante de Refugio' (60 days, renewable) permitting free residence, work, healthcare, education access, and the ability to rent accommodation while the claim is processed; attend a mandatory personal interview (with translator on request); CONARE then grants indefinite residency or denies (with a 15-day reconsideration window); a recognized refugee obtains a foreigner's identity card (cedula) from SEGIP, renewable every 5 years.
requirements.fix_path: File a claim within 90 days of entry at a border post, airport, DIGEMIG office, or CONARE headquarters, attend the personal interview, and await CONARE's determination.

evidence_required.document: Documento Temporal de Solicitante de Refugio

outcome.duration_length: indefinite upon recognition; 60-day renewable temporary document while pending

sources.title: UNHCR Help Bolivia -- CONARE/SECONARE process, Ley 251/2012 and Decreto 1440/2012, application steps, rights during processing, cedula renewal

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Bolivia). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to UNHCR's own Bolivia portal (tier 2), a detailed and specific description of the process, but not the primary statute text itself (Ley 251/2012 was not independently located and fetched in this build). GENUINE, POSITIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING, the same pattern as Paraguay earlier in this session: Bolivia has a real, named domestic refugee law and government body (CONARE/SECONARE), not a UNHCR-only process running outside state law -- in contrast to Algeria, Haiti, Cuba, and Afghanistan built earlier in this dataset. This is one of the more thoroughly documented refugee processes in this dataset, with concrete deadlines (90 days to file, 60-day renewable interim document, 15-day reconsideration window) rather than vague procedural language. leads_to_pr set true with pr_after_months 0 since CONARE's grant is described as 'indefinite residency' directly, not a temporary status requiring further conversion. Separately, Bolivia's own visa taxonomy also names a distinct, narrower 'Humanitarian Visa' (up to 30 days, for trafficking/exploitation victims or medical accompaniment) -- this dataset treats that as a different, short-term administrative visa rather than a substitute for full refugee status determination, and did not build it as a separate file since it is not itself a residency-track route.
